questions.stem: A TV remote control uses which type of electromagnetic radiation to communicate with the television?
questions.explanation: TV remote controls use infrared radiation. They work by line of sight — you must point the remote at the TV because infrared cannot travel through walls or around obstacles easily. Radio waves (option A) are used for WiFi and broadcast signals. Microwaves (option B) are used for mobile phone signals and cooking.

questions.stem: Microwave ovens heat food, while mobile phones also use microwaves. Why is a microwave oven dangerous but a mobile phone is considered safe for normal use?

options.text: They use completely different types of electromagnetic radiation
Microwave ovens use much higher power levels and a frequency specifically absorbed by water molecules in food
Mobile phones use ionising radiation while ovens do not
Microwave ovens produce heat, but mobile phones produce only signals

questions.explanation: Both use microwaves, but at very different power levels and slightly different frequencies. Microwave ovens operate at high power (~1000 W) at a frequency (2.45 GHz) that is efficiently absorbed by water molecules, causing heating. Mobile phones transmit at very low power (~1-2 W). Option A is wrong — both use microwaves. Option C is wrong — microwaves are non-ionising in both cases.

questions.stem: Ultraviolet radiation from the Sun can cause skin cancer. Which safety measure works by absorbing UV radiation before it reaches the skin?
questions.explanation: Sunscreen contains chemicals that absorb UV radiation, preventing it from penetrating the skin and damaging DNA in skin cells. A hat (option A) blocks UV by providing shade but does not absorb it chemically — it is a physical barrier. Staying indoors (option B) avoids exposure entirely. Drinking water (option D) has no effect on UV protection.

questions.stem: A hospital uses gamma rays to sterilise surgical instruments. Why are gamma rays suitable for this purpose?

options.text: Gamma rays heat the instruments to kill bacteria
Gamma rays are ionising and can destroy the DNA of bacteria and viruses, killing them
Gamma rays wash away bacteria from the surface
Gamma rays make the instruments magnetic, repelling bacteria

questions.explanation: Gamma rays are highly ionising — they carry enough energy to damage and destroy the DNA of microorganisms, effectively killing bacteria and viruses without heating or physically touching the instruments. This allows sterilisation of sealed, pre-packaged equipment. Option A is incorrect — gamma sterilisation is a 'cold' process that does not rely on heat.

questions.stem: Optical fibres in broadband internet use which type of electromagnetic radiation to transmit data over long distances?
questions.explanation: Optical fibres transmit data using visible light or infrared radiation. Light enters the fibre and is kept inside by total internal reflection, allowing signals to travel long distances with minimal loss. Radio waves (option A) are used for wireless communication, not fibre optics. X-rays (option D) would be dangerous and impractical for communication.
